summary.text: 今 means “now” or “today,” a temporal use attested in Shang oracle-bone writing. Early forms have a mouth-like upper shape and a lower mark, but what the graph depicts remains disputed.

formation.text: The early graph is commonly described by its visible parts: a mouth-like upper shape and a lower mark. Interpretations of the whole include a mouth-related sign and a wooden clapper; another proposal connects it with groaning or chanting and suggests the graph was reused for “now” because the words sounded alike. The object’s name and that proposed sound match are unknown, so this borrowing account remains unproven. In the later Shuowen analysis, 今 is divided into 亼 and 乁, with 乁 identified as an ancient form of 及; this dictionary analysis does not settle the early graph’s construction. Separately, 今 is documented as a phonetic element in 吟. That later sound role does not establish that groaning or chanting was the original word written by 今.

components.text: Early forms are described as a mouth-like upper shape above a lower mark, sometimes omitted. This is a proposed pictorial reading of the whole graph; the mark’s referent is disputed.
In the received dictionary analysis, 亼 is the first part of 今. This later division does not establish 亼’s role in the early graph.

The received analysis identifies the second part as 乁, an ancient form and variant of 及. This does not make 及 an ancestor of the shape in 今. Another transcription gives 绁; the intended shape and reason for the discrepancy remain unresolved.

history.text: Oracle-bone and bronze forms have a mouth-like upper shape and a lower horizontal mark, sometimes omitted. In seal-script forms, the lower mark bends downward. These graphic changes do not identify what the mark represents.

The received dictionary analysis divides 今 into 亼 and 乁, identifying the latter as an ancient form of 及. Another transcription renders the second part as 绁. This later analysis does not confirm the early graph’s construction.

uncertainties.text: The early graph’s referent and construction remain disputed. Mouth-related and wooden-clapper readings are proposals. Groaning or chanting is also proposed as an earlier word, but is not established as the word originally written by 今.

The name and pronunciation of an object proposed in the mouth-related or clapper readings are not established. The pronunciation of the temporal word 今 cannot supply that missing evidence, so a sound-based borrowing account remains unproven.
A possible connection between 今 and 其 (“this”) has been proposed, but neither a historical relationship nor a semantic path is established.
The cited oracle-bone example has no individual absolute date in the inspected account. It attests early temporal use but does not establish an earlier meaning or a sequence of semantic development.

senses.period: Shang oracle-bone inscription; individual date unresolved
senses.text: The phrase 今夕其雨 attests the temporal meaning “now” or “today.” This is the earliest supported meaning, not proof of a hypothetical original meaning.
今 is also used for “present,” “current,” and “modern era,” but the examples available here do not date how these uses developed from the earlier temporal sense.
One proposal connects the graph with groaning or chanting, but this is not established as the word originally written by 今.

limitations.text: The Shang temporal attestation does not establish a prior sense or a sequence of semantic development. The listed modern meanings do not date when they arose.
The proposed connection to groaning or chanting does not establish that the graph was borrowed to write “now” or “today”; no donor-word pronunciation or sound match is independently established.

overview.text: 今 means “now” or “today,” attested in Shang oracle-bone writing. Early forms show a mouth-like upper shape over a lower mark that bends in seal script; what the graph depicts remains disputed.

components.text: Early forms show a mouth-like top over a lower mark; the mark bends in seal-script forms. Its referent remains disputed.

evidence.text: A mouth 亼 talking about things
Pictograph of sounds coming out of the mouth. The current meaning "today" is a phonetic loan. The original meaning "moan" is now written as 吟.
是時也。从亼从绁。绁，古文及。

Ideogram (指事) – An inverted 曰 (yuē) ("to speak"), hence 亼 with a horizontal stroke at the bottom, so the inverted mouth means "not to speak".
Another theory suggests that it depicts something in the mouth. Maybe the original form of 噤 (OC *ɡrɯmʔ, *ɡrɯms) or 吟 (OC *ŋɡrɯm, *ŋɡrɯms). The derivative 含 (OC *ɡɯːm) refers to the original word.

Etymology not clear. The word's root may be 其 (OC *ɡɯ, “this”) (Schuessler, 2007).
是時也。从亼从绁。绁，古文及。

Etymological analysis: 會意

The database describes oracle-bone and bronze forms as an inverted mouth-like top with a lower horizontal mark, sometimes omitted. It reports that the lower mark bends into the present angular lower shape in small-seal forms. This documents graphic change, while leaving the mark’s referent open: it may represent something held in the mouth or a closed mouth.
evidence.title: 漢字「今」：字形演變

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫, Chinese University of Hong Kong
evidence.text: The entry describes oracle and bronze forms as 亼 above 一, sometimes without the lower stroke. It presents competing interpretations: mouth plus tongue or other mouth-related mark, a graph associated with groaning or chanting and later borrowed for ‘now,’ and Xu Zhongshu’s interpretation of a wooden clapper bell whose sound called people to order. Its account also cites the Shang oracle-bone phrase 今夕其雨 (roughly, ‘Will it rain tonight?’), Heji 20912, and Western Zhou bronze examples. These attest temporal use early; they do not by themselves prove which proposed pictorial account is correct.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：今

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫, Chinese University of Hong Kong
evidence.text: The entry treats 亼 as a downward-open mouth-like component in graphs including 今, and distinguishes the character 亼 from a visually similar graph. This is the source’s analysis of the component, not independent proof that the original depicted object or its spoken name is known.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：亼

evidence.field: 今部 / 說文解字正文及注
evidence.text: The received Shuowen account glosses 今 as ‘this time’ and analyzes it as 从亼从绁, with 绁 identified as 古文及. evidence.text: The entry says oracle-bone and bronze forms combine 亼 with 一, sometimes omitting 一. It surveys competing readings: a mouth with a tongue or other mark; a graph originally associated with groaning or chanting and later used for ‘now’; and Xu Zhongshu’s wooden-clapper interpretation. These are source proposals, not a settled account of the referent.

evidence.text: The page describes oracle-bone and bronze forms as an inverted-mouth-like upper part with a lower horizontal stroke, sometimes omitted. It says the lower stroke becomes a bent line in small-seal forms. This supports a graphic sequence, while leaving the stroke’s referent open.

evidence.field: 今 / received Shuowen wording and Middle Chinese category
evidence.text: The entry quotes the received Shuowen analysis as 今 ‘this time’; 从亼从乁, with 乁 identified as 古文及. It also gives 居吟 as the Guangyun fanqie and classifies the Middle Chinese initial as 見, level tone, 侵 rhyme. This is dictionary tradition, not direct confirmation of a Shang pictorial explanation.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：今

evidence.text: The entry identifies 乁 as 古文及, an ancient form of 及. Together with the received Shuowen wording, this supports identifying the second part of the traditional analysis with 及; it does not establish that 及 is the graphic ancestor of the form in 今.
evidence.title: 漢字「乁」：字義

context.provenance: Base evidence consists of imported local JSONL excerpts. Source names identify upstream datasets; extraction may lose sense and language boundaries. Further external evidence and research activity are documented separately in the dossier.
editorial_rules: Write about the character's graphic history; distinguish it from the history of a spoken word.
Separate historical explanation from mnemonics. Do not infer history from modern shapes or readings.
Sources may repeat one another. A source count is not independent corroboration.
Treat Shuowen as a historical account, not automatic confirmation. Its generated English glosses are excluded.
Unrelated word senses may appear in Wiktionary excerpts. Do not merge them into a character origin.
Related-character evidence retains its record_character. Do not silently transfer a traditional form's components to a simplified form.
No glyph image has been visually inspected in this packet. Do not claim to have inspected one.
Explain missing evidence explicitly, especially for Japanese-created characters. A Chinese spelling pronunciation is not evidence for a Japanese origin.

gaps: The character-specific official Unicode Unihan pages for 亼 (U+4EBC), 今 (U+4ECA), and 吟 (U+541F) could not be retrieved. Local kMandarin rows were checked, but the requested per-character upstream click-through verification is unavailable.

The external Baxter–Sagart PDF was inaccessible. Exact Baxter–Sagart readings above are transcribed from the local TSV rows only; the local 亼 row is absent from that reconstruction table. Keep those readings distinct from the inspected Zhengzhang system.

No inspected source independently establishes the name or pronunciation of the object in either the mouth/tongue or wooden-clapper interpretation. The reconstructed pronunciation of the temporal word 今 does not establish the name of the depicted object or a donor word. Therefore a whole-graph phonetic-loan account remains a proposal, not a demonstrated sound-based borrowing.

The source’s text rendering of the Shuowen component appears as 绁 in one transcription, while the Taiwan dictionary and Academia Sinica identify the form as 乁/ancient 及. No glyph image was visually inspected, so the exact printed shape and whether the differing character is encoding/OCR corruption remain unresolved.

The identified early oracle attestation supports the temporal sense, but the inspected page gives no individual absolute date for Heji 20912. The Western Zhou bronze examples likewise have no individual years in the inspected account.

The proposed relationship between 今 and root 其 (‘this’) is reported by Wiktionary as a possibility attributed to Schuessler; the inspected material did not establish the semantic path or chronological evidence.

The graphic interpretation of 今 remains disputed. The evidence supports later phonetic use of 今 in 吟, but does not settle whether groaning/chanting was the original word written by 今, or whether the bell and mouth interpretations are correct.

Character-specific Unicode Unihan records for U+4ECA, U+4EBC, and U+541F returned errors, so the local kMandarin rows could not be independently checked against official per-character pages. Current Mandarin readings are therefore not asserted as externally verified evidence here.

The local Baxter–Sagart table rows for 今 and 吟 are reported in the dossier as *[k]r[ə]m and *m-qʰ(r)[ə]m respectively; the external PDF was inaccessible in the earlier repository research, and this invocation did not independently retrieve it. They are not treated as externally verified readings. Zhengzhang krɯm and ŋɡrɯm are reported separately above.

No inspected source independently establishes the name or pronunciation of an object depicted by the mouth/tongue or wooden-clapper proposals. A reconstruction of the temporal word 今 cannot establish a donor word for an object, so a whole-graph phonetic-loan account remains unproven.

The Shang oracle inscription cited as Heji 20912 has no individual absolute date in the inspected account. Its temporal sense is early-attested, but the source does not establish an earlier ‘groan/chant’ sense. Later use of 今 as 吟’s phonetic element does not establish the graph’s original referent.

The source text displays Shuowen’s component inconsistently as 绁 versus 乁. Other inspected references identify 乁 as 古文及; whether 绁 reflects encoding, transcription, or OCR corruption remains unresolved.

The Wikimedia Commons original-image links were recorded on inspected pages but their download fetch attempts returned cache-miss errors. Captions therefore describe the source’s labeled vector redraws without claiming pixel inspection.

items.period: Shang dynasty oracle-bone script, source page cites 乙7795 合6834 賓組 (broad period: Late Shang; no more precise date claimed)
items.tradition: Shang oracle-bone script, modern vector redraw referencing Sinica 42.E796
items.caption: This oracle-script form of 今 has an inverted-mouth-like upper shape and a lower horizontal mark. The mark’s referent is uncertain; proposed readings include a mouth-related sign and a wooden clapper.
items.alt: Black line form with an inverted, open triangular upper shape, a horizontal stroke across its lower area, and a separate short stroke below.
items.selection_reason: Shows the early form described in paleographic accounts and makes its debated lower mark visible without assigning it a settled meaning.
items.rights: Commons identifies the image as CC0/public domain; the referenced Xiaoxuetang query glyph image is also explicitly CC0 under the official notice.

items.period: Shuowen seal-script tradition (received dictionary form; not assigned an unsupported artifact date)
items.tradition: Small-seal / Shuowen seal-script style, modern vector redraw referencing Sinica 71.E550
items.caption: In this seal-script form of 今, the lower mark bends downward beneath the upper strokes. Paleographic accounts describe such a change from the horizontal mark in earlier forms; this graphic difference does not settle what the mark originally represented.
items.alt: Black line form with a peaked, open triangular top, a short horizontal interior stroke, and a long bent stroke descending from the center.
items.selection_reason: Adds a distinct seal-script form that illustrates the reported change in the lower mark and helps explain the character’s graphic history.
items.rights: Commons identifies public-domain/CC0 reuse; the referenced Xiaoxuetang query glyph image is covered by the official query-image CC0 notice.

limitations.text: The forms illustrate graphic features, but do not establish what the lower mark depicts. Mouth-related, groaning or chanting, and wooden-clapper explanations remain proposals; the original referent is unresolved.

The early attestation 今夕其雨 shows temporal use of 今, but does not establish an earlier meaning or resolve the graph’s origin. The cited inscription has no individual absolute date in the inspected account.
